t.E321.agn: In its 2012 re-evaluation, EFSA set the acceptable daily intake (ADI) at 0.25 mg/kg body weight; it noted that this limit is unlikely to be exceeded in adults, but that it may be exceeded in high-consuming children (95th percentile) in some countries.
t.E321.body: BHT is absorbed from the intestine, transformed in the liver and excreted from the body.
t.E321.eff.0.t: The daily limit may be exceeded
t.E321.found.0: Fats used in the food industry
t.E321.prod: Produced by chemical synthesis by reacting p-cresol with isobutylene; its raw materials are obtained from petroleum and coal tar.
t.E321.regx.0: Re-evaluated; ADI 0.25 mg/kg body weight/day (raised from the previous 0.05). The ADI may be exceeded in high-consuming children in some countries.
t.E321.summary: A petroleum-derived synthetic antioxidant. It delays rancidity in fats, chewing gum and packaging.
t.E321.what: It is an antioxidant that delays fats spoiling with oxygen and going rancid.
